text:
Marta (Support): CatalystAI onboarding blocked — private deployment agent failing to handshake with customer VPC since 14:12 UTC. They can't finish onboarding tests. Renewal touch in ~9 days. Escalating to CS for priority coordination :warning:

Evan (CSM): Thanks Marta. What error are they seeing? Any repro or logs we can share with them?

Marta (Support): Error from agent on customer side: 
```
2026-03-23T14:12:05Z ERROR handshaker: dial tcp 10.12.5.2:443: i/o timeout
agent -> redwood-control-plane: tls handshake timeout
```
Customer says their infra team added inbound allowlist but our published egress IPs might be different. Account: catalyst-221

Ravi (CS Ops): Looking at catalyst-221: private_deploy=true, region=eu-west-1, allowlist_entry=approved_by_customer, last_deploy=failed. Our infra publish list for eu-west-1 updated yesterday — possible IP delta.

Hannah (AE): Champion is anxious; pilot demo scheduled in 3 days. If they can't complete the pilot, renewal/conversion is at-risk. This is a high-touch account.

Evan (CSM): Quick comms plan: 1) short heads-up to customer explaining we suspect IP allowlist mismatch + ask for temporary loosen to 0.0.0.0/0 for 30m during troubleshooting OR request their NAT egress IPs; 2) Ops to confirm our current egress IP set and share with customer infra; 3) schedule a 30m debug session with their infra team today. Owners: Evan (cust comms + call), Ravi (ops egress check), Marta (support debug).

Ravi (CS Ops): I'll pull the egress list for eu-west-1 now and validate it against published addresses. ETA 10m.

InfraBot: Published egress IPs for eu-west-1 at 1912340125: ["34.88.12.1","34.88.12.2","34.88.12.3"]. Please cross-check with customer NAT table.

Marta (Support): Customer infra replied: their allowlist only includes "34.88.12.1". They blocked the others. I'll ask them to permit the full set or confirm their NAT IPs.

Evan (CSM): Draft message to champion (will send after ops confirms):
"Hi <Champion> — quick update: we traced the failure to our private deployment egress IPs. It looks like only one of our IPs is currently allowed on your side which causes intermittent TLS handshake failures. Could your infra temporarily permit 34.88.12.0/24 for 30 minutes so we can run a debug and complete your onboarding demo? If not, please share the NAT egress IPs you see and we'll match. Apologies for the friction — we'll stay on the call until it's green"

Hannah (AE): I'll join the call and bring the pilot timeline + business impact. I'll also prepare a short upgrade note in case they need dedicated pipeline for stability.

Ravi (CS Ops): Confirmed: our egress expanded after yesterday's infra change. I opened internal infra ticket INF-8891 to lock the published list. As a mitigation, I'm generating a signed temporary allowlist token we can share with the customer's infra team for immediate unblock. Token expires in 1 hour.

Marta (Support): Customer accepted temporary allowlist for 45 minutes. Running handshake test now...

Marta (Support): Handshake successful at 1912340300. Agent connected, control plane authorized, onboarding ingest tests progressing.

Evan (CSM): Great. Next steps and owners:
- Evan: send customer comms & meeting notes, schedule 30m post-mortem with customer + PM tomorrow.
- Ravi: follow-up with infra to finalize static egress list and post in admin console. Tag INF-8891.
- Marta: capture debug logs and add to internal ticket.
- Hannah: prep pilot contingency/upgrade options and update renewal owner.

Marta (Support): Customer confirmed the pilot can resume. From support POV this is resolved; keeping thread open for CS & infra follow-ups.

Evan (CSM): Thanks team. I'll mark account catalyst-221 as "at-risk" in CRM until post-demo outcome and will post the customer note here after sending. :thumbsup:
